cards.text: Meet Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The word of the LORD comes to him, and God calls him Son of man. God says the people around Ezekiel have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear.

cards.question: God says these people have eyes to see and ears to hear, but they don't see or hear. What reason does God give?

cards.text: So God's plan isn't a sermon. It's a one-man SHOW: pack your bags and, in broad daylight, set out from your place to another while they watch.

cards.question: Ezekiel's packing his bags in front of everybody. What kind of trip is God telling him to act out?
God says the people are sure to understand the moment they see Ezekiel's bags come out.

cards.text: Bags out by day, then in the evening he heads out like someone going into exile. And picture this: the front door is RIGHT THERE, everybody's watching, and God tells Ezekiel to dig through the wall and carry his things out through it.

cards.question: At dusk, with his bags on his shoulder, God tells Ezekiel to cover his face. Why?

answers.text: So he cannot see the land

cards.question: God explains what all this acting is for. He has made Ezekiel a ___ to the house of Israel.
Strange orders and all, Ezekiel does exactly as God commanded him.

cards.text: Ezekiel digs through the wall by hand and heads out at dusk with his bags on his shoulder, while everybody watches. Friend, if my neighbor tunneled out of his own house with a suitcase, I'm not calling a contractor. I'm calling the GROUP CHAT.

The next morning, the word of the LORD comes, and God brings up the question the rebellious house asked Ezekiel: 'What are you doing?' Fair question, and I'd have asked it while he was still elbow-deep in the wall.

cards.question: God gives Ezekiel the answer to tell them. Who does this burden concern?

answers.text: The prince in Jerusalem and the people there
The exiles living right there with Ezekiel
The kings of the nations around Israel

cards.question: Ezekiel is to tell them he is a sign. What happened to him will be done to them, and they will go into exile as ___.

cards.text: Then God gets specific: at dusk the prince will lift his bags to his shoulder and go out, they'll dig through the wall to bring him out, and he'll cover his face so he can't see the land. Ezekiel was the rehearsal. THIS is opening night.

cards.question: The prince slips out with his face covered. What does God say He will spread over him?
God says the prince will be brought to Babylon and will see it with his own eyes.

cards.text: The prince will die there, in Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans. His attendants and troops get scattered to every wind with a sword chasing after them, and God says they will know that He is the LORD.

cards.question: God says He will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague. Why?

answers.text: So they can recount their abominations among the nations
So they can rebuild the walls of the city
So they can serve the prince in Babylon

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, with another sign. This one doesn't need a wall. Just a table.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel how to eat his bread and drink his water. How is he supposed to do it?

cards.text: Then Ezekiel tells the people of the land what it means. The people in Jerusalem and the land of Israel will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread.

cards.question: God says the land of Israel will be stripped of everything in it. Why?

answers.text: Because of the violence of all who dwell in it
Because the rain stopped falling for years
Because the prince ran away at dusk

cards.question: God says the cities will stay standing even while the land suffers.

cards.text: Again the word of the LORD comes, this time about a proverb in the land of Israel: 'The days go by, and every vision fails.' That's the snooze button turned into a saying, friend: hit it once, the world doesn't end, so you figure you can hit it FOREVER.

cards.question: When the people say every vision fails, what do they mean?

answers.text: The visions are hard to understand

cards.question: God hears Israel's proverb about failing visions. What does He say He'll do with it?

cards.text: In its place, God gives them a new line: 'The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.' Same 'days,' same 'every vision,' and the ending gets flipped like a cookie box lid.

cards.question: God says false visions and flattering divinations will keep showing up in the house of Israel.
God says whatever word He speaks will be fulfilled without ___.
God tells the rebellious house when He'll bring His message to pass. When?

cards.text: Then a second saying: 'The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.' That's the bill on the counter, friend. Oh, it's real. It's just FUTURE ME's problem.

cards.question: This second saying claims Ezekiel's visions will never happen at all.
What is God's answer to the saying that Ezekiel's vision is for the distant future?

answers.text: None of His words will be delayed any longer
The vision really is for many years from now
He will send another prophet before it comes

cards.text: Snooze button or Future Me, God gives the same answer: 'The message I speak will be fulfilled.' When He says it, you can set your timer by it.

findings.problem: Verses 4-5 are God's commands, but the card tells them as things Ezekiel does ('Bags out by day, then in the evening he heads out like someone going into exile'). That gives away card 9, which asks whether Ezekiel does as he was commanded (12:7).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of 12:7 plus two joke sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The prince in Jerusalem shows up here for the first time, in the right answer and then on card 14, and Papa Dorin never simply says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the long retelling of 12:12, then 'Ezekiel was the rehearsal.' and 'THIS is opening night.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card carries more than two beats: the prince dies in Babylon, his attendants and troops are scattered with a sword chasing them, and they will know that He is the LORD.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'So they can recount their abominations among the nations', uses Bible wording ('recount', 'abominations'). The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 3 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank out of 10 choice cards.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ('Then the word of the LORD comes…', 'This one doesn't need a wall.', 'Just a table.').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card calls the eating and drinking 'another sign', but 12:17-20 never calls it a sign.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card cites Ezekiel 12:17-18, but it only tells 12:17. The content of 12:18 (bread with trembling, water with anxiety) is held back for card 2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The snooze-button joke ('hit it once, the world doesn't end, so you figure you can hit it FOREVER') explains what the proverb means. That gives away card 7, which asks what 'every vision fails' means ('The visions never come true').

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: In 'the ending gets flipped like a cookie box lid', the comparison has a different action. A lid flipping open doesn't reverse anything, while the new line reverses the proverb's meaning. The image doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
